SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_and¶

Back to SeriesTraverseAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseAccessor::find_and(const Series& lhs_mask,
                                               const Series& rhs_mask) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_and(const Series& lhs_mask,
                                            const Series& rhs_mask) const;

The companions find_or and find_not cover the other two boolean combinators.

What It Does¶

find_and(lhs_mask, rhs_mask) returns the coordinates of every position where both masks are true. It is find_all with the mask lhs_mask.logical_and(rhs_mask).

The whole family — find_and, find_or, find_not — exists to combine two conditions you already have as masks without writing an intermediate logical_and / logical_or / logical_not and a separate find_all. When the two conditions are simple comparisons against the same Series, find_btw is often the more direct tool; find_and earns its place when the two masks come from different sources or different logic.

Both masks are interpreted as “non-zero means true” and must match the traversed shape (no broadcasting between the two masks or against the source).

Parameters¶

lhs_mask (const Series&)

The first condition, shaped like the traversed Series.

rhs_mask (const Series&)

The second condition, same shape.

Returns¶

TraverseMatch Row-major coordinates and matched values of the positions satisfying both masks. K can be 0.

Gradient¶

Coordinates carry no gradient. match.values() and match.select_from(other) are differentiable gathers.

Examples¶

Example 1. Positions that are both at least 5 and at most 9.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto hits = grid.traverse.find_and(grid.ge(5.0), grid.le(9.0));

std::cout << "count=" << hits.count() << "\n";
std::cout << hits.coords();
std::cout << hits.values();

Output¶

count=5
pluss::Series(shape=[5,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=10, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 2],
  [1, 1],
  [1, 2],
  [2, 0],
  [2, 2]]
pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[7, 9, 6, 8, 5]

10 fails the upper mask and 4, 2, 1 fail the lower one, so they are excluded.

Example 2. Two masks from different Series: keep positions where grid is high and the aligned cost is low.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});
auto cost = pluss::make_series({
    {9.0, 1.0, 2.0},
    {5.0, 3.0, 8.0},
    {1.0, 6.0, 4.0},
});

auto hits = grid.traverse.find_and(grid.ge(6.0), cost.le(4.0));

std::cout << "count=" << hits.count() << "\n";
std::cout << hits.values();

Output¶

count=3
pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[7, 9, 8]

grid >= 6 at five spots; of those, cost <= 4 only at grid[0,2]=7, grid[1,1]=9, grid[2,0]=8.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Both masks must match the traversed shape exactly. There is no broadcasting.

  • “Non-zero means true” — a non-boolean mask is accepted.

  • When both conditions compare the same Series to constants, prefer find_btw.

  • Coordinates are non-differentiable; values() and select_from() are.

Summary¶

find_and(a, b) finds every position where two masks are both true:

  • convenience over find_all with a logical_and

  • pairs with find_or and find_not

  • exact shape match on both masks

See Also¶

  • find_or: either mask true.

  • find_not: a mask false.

  • find_btw: the direct tool when both conditions bound the same Series.

  • TraverseMatch: the result object.
